summary: Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology who studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of California in 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xueyu (attested 2010).

Yaroslav Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at multiple Tibetan institutions under various traditional teachers, completed graduate research at the University of Virginia, held a Mellon postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University, and worked at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

Yaroslav Vassilkov (born 1943) is an Indologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (~1960–1966). He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1967) and the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University.

Yasuaki Nara (1929–2017) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1956) under Kogen Mizuno. He became professor emeritus at Komazawa University (~1999–2017) and directed the Soto Zen Comprehensive Research Center (attested 2000).

Yasuhiko Nagano (born 1946) is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at UC Berkeley (~1974–1978). He held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1998–2011) and the National Museum of Ethnology, becoming professor emeritus in ~2011.

Yasuhiro Okazaki is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. He held teaching posts at Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda, Kabe, and Takamiya high schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and completed short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library. He held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1979–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996).
Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuke Ikari (born 1940) is an Indologist who studied under Masaaki Hattori and completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (~1969–1978). He held posts at Kindai University, Harvard University, and Kyoto University, where he became professor emeritus in ~2004.

Yasumasa Sekine (born 1949) specializes in religious studies and Indology, having studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1967–1971). His career includes posts at Japan Women's University, Gakushuin Women's College, the University of Tsukuba, and Kwansei Gakuin University (~2014).

Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his degrees at the University of Tokyo and researched at the University of Göttingen. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo and president of the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.

Yasuo Deguchi (born 1962) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1981–1991) and held appointments at Nagoya Institute of Technology (~1996–2006) and Kyoto University, where he was Associate Professor of Philosophy (~2006–2016).

Yasuo Goto is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a lecturer and part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991, 2006) and as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

Yasuo Inamoto (born 1966) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He served as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1996–2007) and took up a post at Kyoto University in ~2007.

Yasuo Matsunami (1946–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He served as a researcher at Taisho University and advisor to the Sravakabhumi Study Group until 2010.
Yasuo Sano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.

Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji, later holding posts at Yamanashi, Osaka, Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University, where he became professor emeritus.

Yasuro Abe (born 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Wako University. He held professorships at Otemae University, Nagoya University (~2003–2018), and Osaka University (attested 2004).
